transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, yeah, so... I guess what finally made me come in is that I just keep forgetting basic adult things. Like, paying my bills, returning interview emails... Oh my god, the emails. I actually had this one recruiter reach out to me for a really great entry-level job, and their company had this super cute logo with a little blue octopus. I love octopuses. I watched this whole documentary about them the other night, and did you know they can open glass jars from the inside? It's wild, they're so smart. 

But, right, anyway—I completely forgot to reply to her. And it's not just that, it's showing up for appointments, or following through on basic errands. I'll leave the house to do one thing and just completely blank on it. It’s just started costing me real opportunities now, and since I just finished my degree, I really need a job, but I just can't seem to keep it together.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Um, no, I don't think so. Like, I get frustrated with myself, obviously, but I don't feel sad or hopeless. And I definitely still like doing my normal stuff. I still get really excited about things! 

Actually, I’ve been super into baking bread lately. Sourdough, specifically. My roommate got me a starter—I named him Dough-Joe—and you have to feed it every day. Which is honestly a miracle that I've kept it alive this long. But yeah, making the bread is so fun. You get to fold the dough and it feels really squishy. Except the other day I left the flour bag open on the counter and we got pantry moths. Have you ever had pantry moths? They are a total nightmare. You have to throw away literally everything in your cabinets, and my roommate was so mad because she had this really expensive organic quinoa... wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, feeling down. No, I'm pretty happy usually, just... a mess.
Do you often feel restless, have trouble staying seated, or find yourself acting impulsively without thinking things through?

Yeah, definitely. Especially the restless part. If I have to sit through something like an interview, or a meeting, or even just a movie, I get this intense pressure inside my body. It's like I physically need to get up or shift around, or at least do something with my hands, otherwise I feel like I'm going to crawl out of my skin. 

Actually, I went to the movies last week with my roommate to see that new sci-fi one. The one with the really cool spaceships? I love sci-fi. My dad used to take me to see all the Star Wars movies when I was a kid, and we'd always get the massive tub of popcorn with the fake butter. The fake butter is the best part, honestly. Real butter just makes it soggy. But anyway, the movie was almost three hours long, and by the second hour, my leg was bouncing so much the guy next to me actually shushed me. I didn't even realize I was doing it! I tried to stop, but then I started picking at my cuticles, and I made one of them bleed, which was super embarrassing. I had to go to the bathroom just to walk around for a minute. Wait, did you ask about impulsivity too? I feel like I just talked for five minutes straight.
When did you first start noticing these difficulties with forgetfulness, restlessness, and impulsivity? Were they present when you were a child, or did they start more recently?

Oh, it's definitely been forever. Like, way back when I was a little kid. I remember in elementary school, my report cards always said the exact same thing. My teachers would write that I was bright, but I was constantly losing my worksheets or rushing through all the directions. And I talked out of turn a lot. Plus, my desk was a complete disaster zone—it was so messy I could literally never find any of my assignments when it was time to turn them in. 

Actually, speaking of messy desks, I tried to organize my room yesterday using this new method I saw on TikTok. It's where you put everything into clear plastic bins so you don't forget what you own. I went to Target to get the bins, but Target is so dangerous, you know? I walked in for storage containers and walked out with a new bath mat, three candles, and a huge bag of those seasonal M&Ms. The peanut butter ones. They are the best. I don't even know why they make the regular milk chocolate ones anymore when peanut butter exists. My roommate is allergic to peanuts, actually, which is a huge bummer because I have to hide my snacks in my closet so I don't accidentally take her out with a candy shell... wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, when it started. But yeah, it's been like this since elementary school for sure.

Do you feel like these difficulties with forgetfulness, restlessness, and staying on task have been significantly interfering with your life — like in school, work, or relationships — not just occasionally causing minor problems?

Yeah, it's... it's ruining everything, honestly. It's definitely not just minor problems anymore. Like, I actually got fired from my last job because I kept missing deadlines and losing track of things. And since then, it's just been a disaster. I've missed follow-up emails for interviews because I open them, think "I'll reply to this after lunch," and then they just vanish from my brain completely. 

Speaking of lunch, I tried making this huge batch of meal-prep salads on Sunday because I saw this video about how eating more leafy greens helps with brain fog. I bought all these fancy containers and this special dressing shaker. But then I forgot to put the chicken in the fridge, so I had to throw it all out. Chicken is so expensive right now, too. My mom was telling me the other day about how much groceries cost when she was my age, and it's actually insane. She used to buy a whole week of groceries for like, fifty bucks. Now fifty bucks gets you a bag of apples and some cheese. I love cheese though. Especially sharp cheddar. 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, how it's affecting my life. Yeah, so I'm unemployed right now because of all this. And I even had to step back from this volunteer project at the animal shelter that I really, really cared about, just because I couldn't keep my schedule straight. I just feel like I can't even manage the basic steps to get my life moving forward. It's really frustrating.
Do these difficulties with forgetfulness, restlessness, and staying on task happen in different places, like at home, at work, and in public, or are they mostly limited to one setting?

It's everywhere, honestly. It's not just one place. Like, at home, I'm constantly losing my phone or my keys, or I'll start doing laundry and then get distracted by a book and totally forget about the wet clothes until they smell weird. And then I have to wash them again. I actually had to wash the same load of towels three times last week. They were these really nice, fluffy towels my aunt got me for graduation. She got me this whole matching set—bath towels, hand towels, washcloths, everything. They're this really pretty seafoam green color, which is my favorite. I actually wanted to paint my bedroom that color, but my landlord is super strict about not painting the walls. He's this older guy who always complains about the landscaping. He actually yelled at me once because my roommate left her bike on the grass. Which wasn't even my fault! She's the one who rides her bike everywhere because she's trying to save money on gas. Gas prices are ridiculous right now. 

But, um... wait, where does it happen? Yeah, so home is a mess. And work, well, obviously I told you about getting fired from my last job because I couldn't keep track of things there. And even just out in public, like at the grocery store or the movies, I'm always fidgeting or forgetting why I walked down an aisle. So yeah, it's pretty much everywhere I go. It never really stops.
